title: Recover Binary Search Tree
prompt:
You are given the `root` of a binary search tree in which exactly two nodes had their values accidentally swapped. Recover the tree without changing its overall structure, so that it becomes a valid BST again.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it. Return the corrected tree serialized to a level-order array using the provided `tree_to_level_order` helper.

examples.explanation: Nodes 1 and 3 were swapped; swapping their values back produces a valid BST.
Nodes 2 and 3 were swapped; correcting them restores BST order.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [2, 1000]
It is guaranteed that exactly two nodes of the tree have been swapped
hints: An in-order traversal of a valid BST visits values in strictly increasing order — a swap creates one or two places where a value is followed by a smaller one.

Walk the in-order traversal while comparing each node to the previous one. If the swapped nodes are adjacent in the in-order sequence, there is exactly one such violation, spanning both swapped nodes; if they're not adjacent, there are two separate violations.

Track the first node involved in the first violation and the second node involved in the last violation seen — those two nodes are exactly the ones that need their values swapped back, regardless of whether one or two violations were found.

solution.approach: Perform an in-order traversal, keeping a reference to the previously visited node. Compare each node's value to the previous one: whenever a decrease is found, it signals a BST violation. The first violation's earlier node is always the first misplaced node; the later node in the (possibly second) violation is always the second misplaced node. Track 'first' on the first violation encountered, and continuously update 'second' on every violation seen (so it ends up as the later node of the last violation). After the traversal, swap first.val and second.val to restore the BST property without changing tree structure.
